title: Baby Broadcaster
subtitle: The good news is we found a radio station. The bad news? The host hasn't learned to speak yet.

items.text: They get out of the car and step onto the asphalt road.
A barely perceptible moisture fills the air. The mist is pervasive, even filling their ears and nostrils.
A faint breeze runs along their faces, like a spider's web blowing in the wind.
A flash of insight comes to her from some distant, unreachable place.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What is it, Captain?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Someone's casting arcane skills nearby.
*baby cries*
The crying of a baby throbs faintly in her ears like an insect bite.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you hear that? Sounds like a crying baby.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Better go take a look.
The grass is rustling, as if something is moving nearby.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You know, a Texan soldier once told me about a notorious bandit back in his hometown many years ago.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: He would record the sound of a crying baby and play it outside the homes of single mothers. Then he'd wait, ready to attack them if any of them opened their door to look for the baby.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, but the actions of one man don't negate all other calls for help.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Of course not. It's just a reminder to be ready for anything. We're close now. Prepare yourself.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Got it.
The grass sways, and the faint crying stops. The fog grows thicker.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Vertin, over here!
A broken flashlight lies on the ground. The damage looks recent.
Not far away, they spot a foot in a black shoe, and a pale ankle disappearing under purple fabric.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Ah. Hello. Please help.
A frail woman tightly cradles a swaddled infant, her body curled up and trembling with fear.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are you alright, Miss?
The maid turns her head. Her face is pale, as if all the blood has been drained from it.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Finally, someone ...

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Please, help me. These critters won't let me leave. Every time I try, they knock me back.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: My baby's starving and crying. If you hadn't come, I really don't know what I would've done.

items.speaker: Mummus
items.text: Cooumm, cooumm ... Urhm, urhm ...
The critter makes a wary sound.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You mean these Mummus? I've never read about them attacking anyone in any reports. In fact, they're known for being rather timid.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Reports don't necessarily capture the whole story, Captain.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Look at them. They don't seem very "timid" to me.

items.speaker: Mummus
items.text: Coo ...
The Mummus before them opens its mouth wide, revealing its sharp white teeth.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Careful! It's going to attack!
The creatures scatter, the grass rustling as they flee.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Ah. They always run off so quickly.
The woman pulls herself up off the ground and brushes the dirt from her skirt.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are you alright?

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Did you get a good look at them? Those slippery little things look like seals, don't they?

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: They always jump on passing cars and rub their flat hind legs on the roof, making that coarse scraping sound.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Amazing creatures, aren't they? These little fearmongers.
Wind sweeps across the plains, dispersing the fog. The woman's face flushes red as she sways lightly in the breeze.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: But they are, in fact, easily frightened; the slightest movement could startle them. That's why it's foggy all year around here. Many of my guests have trouble finding their way to the motel.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Are you ladies looking to check in at the motel?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Motel?

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Yes, Tuesday's Motel. If you're looking for a comfortable bed for the night, it's the place to go.

items.speaker: Maid
items.text: Anyway, thank you so much for saving us. I owe you one.
She pats the swaddled baby.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Excuse me, are you the maid at Tuesday's Motel?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ah, I almost forgot to introduce myself. Folks around here call me Tuesday.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: "Hey, Tuesday, over here. Hey, Tuesday! Breakfast for one, please. Tuesday, Tuesday ..." Ain't we all like horses, and our names like the reins pulling at us?
She looks the two of them over.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Do you need a place to stay, ladies?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you for your kindness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But our driver's still in the car. We can't just leave him there.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And our luggage and travel documents are still in the trunk, along with our cash, too. Let's head back now that the fog has cleared.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Shall I lead the way?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: You?
She looks the maid up and down suspiciously.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What were you doing out here alone, anyway?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I-I was waiting for a guest. It's been two hours, and they still haven't shown up.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I thought, rather than waiting here, I would pay you back for helping me.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I assume you parked near Route 77? Let me take you there.
The setting sun scatters its light, illuminating the dogwood and cotton plants in the fields.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: That coward!
The car is gone. Nothing remains but a few scattered pieces of luggage.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: He just threw out our luggage and took off! Tsk, how pathetic.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: At least he didn't take the luggage with him.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Mmm. Are you going to thumb a ride with all these bags?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I'd advise against that, especially here. You've seen those movies, right? Bad things can happen on the road out here.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: There are a lot of smugglers around these days.
There's a clear concern in her voice.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Did you say your motel wasn't far from here?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Yes. Come this way. There's an easy trail that won't dirty your shoes.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Don't worry. It ain't far.
Entrance, Tuesday's Motel
The walk isn't far, indeed. Before long, they're standing in front of the motel.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: When night falls and the signs are lit, a weary traveler may find a comfortable place to rest here.
Under the shade of the neem trees, the wooden porch awaits its owner, darkening in the fading sunlight.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Welcome to Tuesday's Motel, ladies.
